content:
matt: Heads-up — canary telemetry shows a sharp token/sec drop starting around the merge of PR #4521. Throughput down ~20% on gptx-8k workloads. :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: Perf check failed for rollout canary-2026-03-18. tokens_per_sec: baseline=12.4k, canary=9.8k (-21%). See /ci/perf/1793456789.

anika: Ugh. Is this regression reproducible locally or only on canary? Any CI perf job logs? :eyes:

matt: Repro on local with same config (dedicated pool, batch_window=80ms). Ran the bench harness: `./bench --model gptx-8k --concurrency 16` -> token/sec drop consistent.

liam: Starting git bisect now. last known-good tag is v2026-03-10, bad is HEAD (includes #4521). Will post bisect result.

liam: bisect result: first bad commit is 3c1f9b7 (author: anika) — change in scheduler: "normalize_batch_keys() to dedupe cache keys" from PR #4521.

maria: Quick profile (pprof CPU) from local repro attached: top stacks show scheduler spinning in `select_batch_target()` and increased time in `kv_cache::lookup()` around the batching boundary. Paste:```
Flat profile:
  32.4%  scheduler::select_batch_target
  18.7%  kv_cache::lookup
  10.5%  kernel_selector::choose_kernel (fallback path)
  5.2%   memcpy
```

matt: That `kernel_selector::choose_kernel (fallback path)` line stood out to me — commit 3c1f9b7 also changed the key normalization which can alter sequence-length grouping => kernel hints different. If batching windows combine different sequence-lengths, kernel fallback could get chosen more often.

anika: Hmm. The change was meant to dedupe cache keys (fixes duplication in prefix cache), but maybe we broke the canonicalization semantics used by the scheduler. I pushed that PR quickly to reduce duplicate KV entries; didn't think it would influence grouping heuristics.

jen: Observed KV hitrate drop on canary metrics: before merge kv_hitrate=0.78, after kv_hitrate=0.54. That would explain more KV lookups and lower tokens/sec. Can anyone confirm the normalization produced distinct keys for same logical prefix?

maria: Yes — sample keys show toggling of a trailing sentinel token after normalization. Example: before: `req|user:A|ctx_len:64`, after: `req|user:A|ctx_len:64|sentinel:0` in some cases. So cache once-miss pattern appears.

liam: If the KV hitrate went down, batching will see more variable seq lengths in-flight (KV misses force prefix expansion) and kernel selector could move to a slower kernel. That compounds.

matt: Reproduced kernel decision flip locally: with old key canonicalization kernel_selector picks `fast_gpt_kernel_v2`, with new keys it picks `generic_kernel_fallback`. Profiling shows generic path ~1.26x slower on 8k.

anika: Action plan: hold rollout, bisect confirmed 3c1f9b7 is causal. Options: revert PR #4521, or patch normalization to preserve canonical ordering for scheduler. Revert is fastest.

ops-bot: Rollout canary paused by ops (reason: perf regression).

jen: I'll open a quick revert PR and request expedited review. Also we should add a unit test asserting stable canonical key output for identical logical inputs.

liam: Suggestion: short-term mitigation — reduce batch_window to 40ms on canary to force tighter grouping; may increase latency but could avoid kernel fallback. We tested this locally: tokens/sec recovered to ~11.8k (closer to baseline) with batch_window=40ms on the patched build.

matt: Good idea. But we risk masking root cause. I'm in favor of revert + test + reapply with normalization fix.

anika: Agreed. Revert coming. Sorry team — I missed the kernel-selection coupling in my code review. Will follow up with fix and tests.

maria: For postmortem: capture pprof traces from before/after, KV key diffs, and kernel selection logs. We should also add a perf CI that runs short conv workloads and asserts tokens/sec not degrade >5%.

liam: Revert PR: #4568 (revert 3c1f9b7) opened, linking this thread. cc @matt @anika for review.

deploy-bot: Revert PR #4568 bumped to canary-rollback job. Running perf validation.

deploy-bot: Perf validation result: tokens_per_sec: canary-rollback=12.2k, baseline=12.4k (-1.6%). KV_hitrate restored to 0.76.

matt: Thanks — rolling out the revert to full canary. Leaving canary paused until we confirm stability for 30min.

anika: I'll work on an alternative normalization patch that preserves the scheduler-facing canonicalization and add unit + integration tests (kv hitrate smoke).

jen: I'll update the rollout checklist to include a quick perf smoke for kernel selection and KV hitrate whenever key-related changes merge.

matt: Nice catch everyone. Postmortem notes: root cause = key normalization change accidentally added non-deterministic sentinel behavior -> KV misses -> more variable batching -> kernel fallback chosen -> tokens/sec drop.

ops-bot: Canary rollback completed. Monitoring metrics at /dash/perf/canary.

matt: Closing loop — full rollout resumed after 45m. Will keep an eye tonight. :thumbsup:
